coverage_limits: The report covers only the included-study lists of three meta-analyses, whose searches end on 2 May 2025 (Holzner, Maier, and Feuerriegel), in January 2025 (de Rooij and Biskjaer, ECCE 2025) and on 25 Feb 2026 (de Rooij and Biskjaer, homogenization). It could not open the Behaviour & Information Technology and ECCE 2026 full texts, the Tilburg record of the MIC abstract, the SSRN or ScienceDirect abstracts of Castelo, Zheng, Zou & Zhu and Zhou et al., or Bohren's EconStor handle, and it found no DOI or URL for Bangerl et al. 2024.

candidates.title: AI Suggestions Homogenize Writing Toward Western Styles and Diminish Cultural Nuances
candidates.evidence: Writers working without AI are compared with writers given GPT-4o suggestions, and the outcome is group-level homogenization of the writing during AI use. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 (homogenization), coded as a randomized ('controlled') study, although the report notes that the abstract does not describe how participants were assigned.

candidates.title: Homogenization Effects of Large Language Models on Human Creative Ideation
other_versions: doi 10.1145/3613905.3651088 (CHI EA '24 paper on the same study: 'Evaluating Creativity Support Tools via Homogenization Analysis')
candidates.evidence: People generating ideas with ChatGPT-3.5 are compared with people using Oblique Strategies instead, and the outcome is group-level homogenization of ideas during use. The abstract describes a 36-participant comparative user study, and de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 (homogenization) include it as one randomized ('controlled') study reported in two papers (CHI EA '24 and C&C '24).

candidates.title: How AI Ideas Affect the Creativity, Diversity, and Evolution of Human Ideas: Evidence From a Large, Dynamic Experiment
candidates.task: idea generation after seeing example ideas (divergent thinking)
candidates.evidence: Participants generated ideas after seeing six human example ideas or a mix of GPT-3.5 and human examples (four plus two, or two plus four), and the abstract describes varied AI-exposure conditions. Holzner et al. 2025 enter it as HAI12 (AI vs human output, creativity), and de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 enter it as a randomized ('controlled') homogenization study of divergent thinking during AI use.

candidates.title: Evaluating AI-assisted creative ideation: A crossover study in higher education
candidates.task: creative idea generation in higher education
candidates.evidence: In a randomised crossover study in higher education, participants generated ideas with and without ChatGPT-3.5, and the outcome entered is group-level homogenization of ideas during AI use. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 (homogenization), coded 'controlled'.

candidates.title: Explorations in human vs. generative AI creative performances: A study on human-AI creative potential
candidates.evidence: Alternate uses task responses from student dyads are compared with responses from 10 generative AI models, and no participant used AI. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025 (AI vs human output), and the report found no DOI or URL for this workshop paper, so doi and url are null.

candidates.title: Creative and Strategic Capabilities of Generative AI: Evidence from Large-Scale Experiments
candidates.evidence: Per the paper body, participants were randomly assigned to HumanBaseline, HumanAgainstAI or HumanPlusAI conditions, with AI use optional in HumanPlusAI. Included only in Holzner et al. 2025, as HAI08 (AI vs human output, 2 effect sizes) and CP02 (creativity, people with vs without AI). Holzner cites EconStor hdl:10419/305744, which the report could not open.

candidates.title: The Crowdless Future? Generative AI and Creative Problem-Solving
candidates.evidence: Per the abstract, crowd solutions are compared with GPT-4 solutions that the researchers prompted, so no participant used AI. Holzner et al. 2025 enter it as CP12 (creativity, people with vs without AI, 2 effect sizes) and de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025 as AI vs human output (crowd vs GPT-4). Holzner's Table 2 shows its working-paper title, and the title here is from the reference list.

candidates.title: How AI Outperforms Humans at Creative Idea Generation
candidates.evidence: GPT-4 ideas are compared with ideas from experts (app ideas in S1 and product-invention ideas in S2, per the ECCE description), and no participant used AI. Entered as AI vs human output by Holzner et al. 2025 (HAI13) and de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025 (S1, S2), but ECCE cites the title and DOI of a different paper (Li, Castelo, Katona & Sarvary, Marketing Science 43(2):254–266), and the report could not confirm that ECCE's studies are this SSRN paper or reach its abstract.

candidates.title: Creativity and AI
candidates.evidence: Creative output from students is compared with output from GPT-3.5 (S1) and GPT-4 (S2), and no participant used AI. Entered as AI vs human output by Holzner et al. 2025 (HAI09, 4 effect sizes) and de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025 (S1, S2). The report does not describe the task.

candidates.title: Large Language Model in Creative Work: The Role of Collaboration Modality and User Expertise
candidates.task: writing with GPT-4 feedback or example texts
candidates.evidence: Participants wrote with or without an LLM, with GPT-4 giving feedback or example texts depending on the collaboration modality. Holzner et al. 2025 enter it as HAI14 (AI vs human output), CP09 (creativity) and CD04 (diversity, from group means and SDs of cosine distance, 2 effect sizes), and de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 as a randomized ('controlled') homogenization study of writing during AI use.

candidates.title: Writing, creativity, and artificial intelligence. ChatGPT in the university context
candidates.evidence: Per the abstract, ChatGPT output is compared with university students' writing in a non-experimental design, with an added quasi-experimental pre/post phase. Included only in Holzner et al. 2025 as an AI vs human output comparison (2 effect sizes), labelled HAI22 in Table 2 but HAI21 in the forest plot and data files.

candidates.title: Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces the collective diversity of novel content
candidates.evidence: In an online experiment, writers received one or five GPT-4 ideas or none, and outcomes are the creativity of each text and the similarity among texts. Holzner et al. 2025 enter it as CP05 (creativity, 2 effect sizes) and CD01 (diversity, regression coefficients on cosine similarity, 2 effect sizes), and de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 as a randomized ('controlled') homogenization study of writing. Holzner's Table 2 shows a wrong title, and the title here is from the reference list.

other_versions: doi 10.2139/ssrn.5013086 (SSRN working paper, 2024, by Doshi, Chai & Troebinger: 'How Experience Moderates the Impact of Generative AI Ideas on the Research Process')
candidates.evidence: The SSRN abstract describes a pre-registered randomized online experiment with 310 researchers, some given generative-AI ideas and some not. Holzner et al. 2025 enter the SSRN version as CP06 (creativity) and CD02 (diversity, regression coefficients on cosine similarity). The report says the Research Policy 2026 version (Tröbinger, Doshi & Chai) has a new title but does not give it, so title is null.

candidates.title: Revolution or inflated expectations? Exploring the impact of generative AI on ideation in a practical sustainability context
candidates.evidence: Per the abstract, AI-based ideation is compared with an expert workshop at one firm, and assignment is not described. Holzner et al. 2025 enter it as HAI17 (AI vs human output) and CP11 (creativity, people with vs without AI), and de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025 as AI vs human output (experts vs GPT-4).

candidates.title: A Confederacy of Models: a Comprehensive Evaluation of LLMs on Creative Writing
candidates.evidence: Creative writing by LLMs is evaluated against human writing, and no participant used AI. Included only in Holzner et al. 2025 as HAI01 (AI vs human output, 12 effect sizes), which cites the arXiv version.

candidates.title: Artificial Creativity? Evaluating AI Against Human Performance in Creative Interpretation of Visual Stimuli
candidates.evidence: AI performance is compared with human performance on creative interpretation of visual stimuli, and no participant used AI. Included only in Holzner et al. 2025 as HAI04 (AI vs human output).

candidates.title: Artificial muses: Generative artificial intelligence chatbots have risen to human-level creativity
candidates.evidence: Alternate uses task responses from a human crowd are compared with responses from five AI models, and no participant used AI. Entered as AI vs human output by Holzner et al. 2025 (HAI05) and de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025.

candidates.title: The current state of artificial intelligence generative language models is more creative than humans on divergent thinking tasks
candidates.evidence: Human responses on divergent thinking tasks are compared with GPT-4 responses, and no participant used AI. Entered as AI vs human output by Holzner et al. 2025 (HAI18, 5 effect sizes) and de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025 (alternate uses task, crowd vs GPT-4).

candidates.title: Evaluating Creative Short Story Generation in Humans and Large Language Models
candidates.evidence: Short stories from 60 LLMs are compared with stories from 60 people, and there is no human-with-AI condition. Holzner et al. 2025 enter it as HAI11 (AI vs human output) and also as CD03 (diversity, people with vs without AI, regression coefficients on cosine similarity), which the report flags as a coding error.

candidates.title: Best humans still outperform artificial intelligence in a creative divergent thinking task
candidates.evidence: Alternate uses task responses from a human crowd are compared with responses from three AI models, and no participant used AI. Entered as AI vs human output by Holzner et al. 2025 (HAI06) and de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025.

candidates.title: Human Creativity in the Age of LLMs: Randomized Experiments on Divergent and Convergent Thinking
candidates.evidence: Participants did divergent thinking tasks with a GPT-4o idea list, with GPT-4o SCAMPER help, or without AI, and the abstract describes randomized experiments. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 (homogenization), with homogenization measured during and after AI use, and the effect was digitized from graphs.

candidates.title: Creative or Uncreative Partner: Comparing Humans and AI in Collaborative Creative Tasks
candidates.evidence: Participants were randomly assigned to write with a human partner or a GPT-4o partner, and the outcome entered is group-level homogenization of the writing. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 (homogenization), coded 'controlled' and marked as not peer-reviewed.

candidates.title: An empirical investigation of the impact of ChatGPT on creativity
candidates.evidence: Creativity of work done with and without ChatGPT is compared across experiments, including divergent thinking (2a) and idea generation (2b). Holzner et al. 2025 enter it as HAI03 (AI vs human output) and CP01 (creativity, 6 effect sizes), de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025 enter Study 2b only (crowd vs GPT-3.5), and experiments 2a and 2b reach de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 through Meincke, Nave & Terwiesch's reanalysis. Lee & Chung's abstract does not say assignment was random, but Meincke et al.'s preprint describes the experiments as randomized.

candidates.title: The Roles of Idea Generation and Elaboration in Human-AI Collaborative Creativity
other_versions: PsyArXiv version 2 (same DOI with suffix _v2), cited by the Behaviour & Information Technology version of de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026
candidates.evidence: Writing with GPT-3.5 access is compared with writing without it, and the outcome entered is group-level homogenization. de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 (homogenization) code it 'controlled' and mark it as not peer-reviewed, but the abstract calls it a naturalistic study, so random assignment is unclear.

candidates.title: Partnering with Generative AI: Experimental Evaluation of Human-Led and Model-Led Interaction in Human-AI Co-Creation
candidates.evidence: Participants generated ideas with GPT-4.1 in three interaction modes or without it, and the abstract describes a randomized controlled experiment. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 (homogenization), marked as not peer-reviewed and citing the 2025 arXiv version. The report gives one title for the arXiv and CHI '26 versions.

candidates.title: Can AI Enhance its Creativity to Beat Humans ?
candidates.evidence: Students' output is compared with GPT-4 output and with output from GPT-4 combined with DALL·E 2, and no participant used AI. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025 (AI vs human output). The report does not describe the task.

candidates.title: Establishing the importance of co-creation and self-efficacy in creative collaboration with artificial intelligence
candidates.authors: McGuire, De Cremer, Van de Cruys
candidates.evidence: The abstract reports two experimental studies of creative collaboration with AI but does not state random assignment. Included only in Holzner et al. 2025, as HAI10 (AI vs human output) and CP03 (creativity, people with vs without AI, 3 effect sizes).

candidates.title: If ChatGPT can do it, where is my creativity? generative AI boosts performance but diminishes experience in creative writing
candidates.evidence: The abstract describes an experimental design in which creative writing with generative AI is compared with a control group, without saying how participants were assigned. Included only in Holzner et al. 2025 as CP07 (creativity, people with vs without AI).

candidates.title: Using Large Language Models for Idea Generation in Innovation
candidates.evidence: Ideas from students, collected before LLMs were available, are compared with GPT-4 ideas, and no participant used AI. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025 (AI vs human output). The report gives no DOI, only a PDF link.

candidates.title: ChatGPT decreases idea diversity in brainstorming
candidates.evidence: Reanalyzes Lee & Chung's experiments 2a (divergent thinking) and 2b (idea generation), comparing the diversity of ideas from people with GPT-3.5 and without AI. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 (homogenization, two entries, coded 'controlled'). The report says its preprint abstract describes the experiments as randomized but gives no identifier for that preprint.

candidates.title: Impersonal Statements: LLM-Era College Admissions Essays Exhibit Deep Homogenization Despite Lexical Diversity
other_versions: doi 10.17605/OSF.IO/P58K3 (OSF record cited by the PsyArXiv version of de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026; it resolves to osf.io/p58k3, listed there as '(a Replication Study)')
candidates.evidence: College admissions essays written before versus after ChatGPT are compared for homogenization, and no one was assigned to AI. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 as a quasi-experiment, marked as not peer-reviewed. The PsyArXiv DOI used here is the one that meta-analysis's journal version cites, while its preprint cites the OSF record listed in other_versions.

candidates.title: The Language of Creativity: Evidence from Humans and Large Language Models
candidates.evidence: Creative output from humans is compared with output from LLMs, and no participant used AI. Included only in Holzner et al. 2025 as an AI vs human output comparison (2 effect sizes), labelled HAI20 in Table 2 but HAI19 in the forest plot and data files. The report does not describe the task.

candidates.title: Does Writing with Language Models Reduce Content Diversity?
candidates.evidence: People wrote with GPT-3 or InstructGPT assistance or without it, and the outcome is group-level content homogenization. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 (homogenization, coded 'controlled'), which computed the effect from the study's raw data. The report gives no DOI for the ICLR version.

candidates.title: Open and closed-ended problem solving in humans and AI: The influence of question asking complexity
candidates.evidence: Problem-solving responses from a human crowd are compared with GPT-4 responses, and no participant used AI. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025 (Study 3 only, AI vs human output).

candidates.title: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
candidates.evidence: Research ideas from expert NLP researchers are compared with ideas from Claude 3.5, and no participant used AI. Entered as AI vs human output by Holzner et al. 2025 (HAI07) and de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025. The title says 100+ researchers, which is not an exact count, so n_participants is null.

candidates.title: Interactions with generative AI chatbots: unveiling dialogic dynamics, students' perceptions, and practical competencies in creative problem-solving
candidates.venue: Int J Educ Technol High Educ 22
candidates.evidence: Per the abstract, quasi-experiments compare students solving creative problems with a generative AI chatbot against students working with peers. Included only in Holzner et al. 2025 as CP08 (creativity, people with vs without AI).

candidates.title: Putting GPT-3's Creativity to the (Alternative Uses) Test
candidates.evidence: Alternate uses task responses from students are compared with GPT-3 responses, and no participant used AI. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025 (AI vs human output). The report gives no DOI for the ICCC version.

candidates.title: Large Language Models show both individual and collective creativity comparable to humans
candidates.evidence: Creative output from students is compared with output from five LLMs, at the individual and collective level per the title, and no participant used AI. Entered as AI vs human output by Holzner et al. 2025 (HAI15, 52 effect sizes) and de Rooij & Biskjaer ECCE 2025. The report does not describe the task.

candidates.title: The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking
candidates.task: visual design with Midjourney image examples
candidates.evidence: In a between-participants study (N = 60), people doing a visual design task with Midjourney image examples are compared with people without generative AI, and the outcome entered is group-level homogenization of designs. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 (homogenization, coded 'controlled'), which digitized the effect from graphs.

candidates.title: Diverse AI personas can mitigate the homogenization effect in human-AI collaborative ideation
other_versions: arXiv 2504.13868 (v1 titled 'Using Generative AI Personas Increases Collective Diversity in Human Ideation')
candidates.evidence: Writers received one or five o1-preview story plots or none, and the outcome entered is group-level homogenization of their writing. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 (homogenization, coded 'controlled'), marked as not peer-reviewed and citing arXiv v1.

candidates.title: We're Different, We're the Same: Creative Homogeneity Across LLMs
candidates.evidence: LLM creative output is compared with human output, with homogeneity across LLMs as the theme per the title, and no participant used AI. Included only in Holzner et al. 2025 as an AI vs human output comparison (3 effect sizes), labelled HAI21 in Table 2 but HAI20 in the forest plot and data files. The report does not describe the task.

candidates.title: One Does Not Simply Meme Alone: Evaluating Co-Creativity Between LLMs and Humans in the Generation of Humor
candidates.evidence: Per the abstract, humor (meme) output is compared across human-only, human-AI and AI-only groups of 50, and assignment is not stated. Included only in Holzner et al. 2025 as HAI16 (AI vs human output). The report does not say whether 50 counts people or memes, so n_participants is null.

candidates.title: AI Delivers Creative Output but Struggles with Thinking Processes
candidates.evidence: AI creative output is compared with human output, and no participant used AI. Included only in Holzner et al. 2025 as HAI02 (AI vs human output, 6 effect sizes). The report does not describe the task.

candidates.title: Large Language Model in Ideation for Product Innovation: An Exploratory Comparative Study
candidates.evidence: An exploratory comparative study of an LLM in product-innovation ideation. The abstract was unreachable, so the report could not check how participants were assigned. Included only in Holzner et al. 2025 as CP10 (creativity, people with vs without AI).

candidates.title: Generative artificial intelligence, human creativity, and art
candidates.evidence: Artworks made before versus after AI adoption are compared for homogenization, and no one was assigned to AI. Included only in de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026 as a quasi-experiment.

candidates.title: Creative scar without generative AI: Individual creativity fails to sustain while homogeneity keeps climbing
candidates.task: research papers (Study 1), divergent thinking and idea tasks (Study 2)
candidates.evidence: Study 1 compares research papers before versus after ChatGPT (quasi-experiment). Study 2 compares ChatGPT-4 with no AI on divergent thinking and idea tasks, with homogenization measured during and after AI use, coded 'controlled'. Both enter de Rooij & Biskjaer 2026. The report took this design from a search-engine snippet because the article page was unreachable, and it notes that the meta-analysis cites volume 75 (2025) while Crossref gives volume 84 (March 2026).

candidates.title: Generative AI Adoption in Human Creative Tasks: Experimental Evidence
other_versions: doi 10.2139/ssrn.5196748 (SSRN working paper, 2025, authors listed as Zou & Zhu)
candidates.evidence: An experiment on generative AI adoption in creative tasks. The abstract was unreachable, so the report could not check how participants were assigned. Holzner et al. 2025 enter the SSRN version as CP04 (creativity, people with vs without AI), and the report gives no separate title for the 2026 journal version, so the SSRN title is used.

candidates.title: Generative AI and Creativity: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of 28 between-subject experiments (127 effect sizes, 8,214 participants in total, search to 2 May 2025). Pooled Hedges' g is −0.048 for GenAI vs human output, 0.273 for the creativity of humans with vs without GenAI (21 effect sizes), and −0.863 for their diversity (6 effect sizes from 4 studies). Only arXiv v1 exists, and data and code are at github.com/SM2982/Meta-Analysis-LLMs-Creativity.

candidates.title: Has AI Surpassed Humans in Creative Idea Generation? A Meta-Analysis
candidates.venue: ECCE '25, Proceedings of the 36th Annual Conference of the European Association of Cognitive Ergonomics (Tallinn), Article 10, pp. 1–11
other_versions: PsyArXiv preprint version 2 (same DOI with suffix _v2)

MIC 2025 one-page abstract: Biskjaer & de Rooij, 'Generative AI has not (yet?) surpassed humans in creative idea generation: A meta-analysis (2022-2025)', 9th MIC Conference, Bolzano, 3–6 Sep 2025, no DOI (Tilburg portal: Accepted/In press)
candidates.task: meta-analysis of AI vs human idea generation
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of 15 articles (17 studies, 115 effect sizes, search window January 2022 to January 2025) comparing human ideas with ideas from GenAI prompted alone, rated blind on creativity, originality or usefulness. Pooled d is .360 [−.071, .790] (positive favors GenAI), co-creation is excluded, and diversity is not analyzed. OSF materials are at osf.io/2xdba.

candidates.title: Does generative AI make us think alike? A systematic review and meta-analysis of homogenisation effects in human–AI co-creation
candidates.venue: Behaviour & Information Technology, e-pub 31 Aug 2026, pp. 1–14
other_versions: doi 10.31234/osf.io/rz5s4_v1 (PsyArXiv preprint dated 15 Apr 2026: 'Does Generative AI Make Us Think Alike? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Homogenization Effects in Human–AI Co-Creation')
doi 10.1145/3822301.3822304 (ECCE 2026 short paper, Siena, pp. 198–201, 14 Sep 2026: 'Generative AI Makes Creative Output More Homogeneous')
candidates.task: meta-analysis of homogenization in human–AI co-creation
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of 19 studies from 18 articles (61 effect sizes, search 2022 to 25 Feb 2026) comparing GenAI users with non-users on group-level homogenization of creative output. Pooled d is .334 [.094, .574] (positive means more homogeneous with AI), with .453 during co-creation and .414 after AI use. The report read the preprint in full, and the journal and ECCE 2026 full texts were unreachable, but their abstracts and reference lists agree with the preprint.
